items.text: The war with the Islamic Republic and its economic consequences, including rising fuel prices and living costs, have become a key issue in the US midterm elections. It has been discussed how much Democrats could limit Donald Trump's policies towards Tehran if they gain control of one or both houses of Congress. An interview with Omid Memarian and Behnam Taleblou has been conducted on this topic.

The Iran Human Rights Organization reported that at least 77 people were executed in Iran in October. Six were executed on security charges and three detainees from the nationwide protests in Dey month were executed during this period. Additionally, at least 691 executions have been recorded in the past 10 months, including three males under 18 at the time of their alleged crimes, 23 women, and 28 foreign nationals.

In one of the voting districts in Virginia Beach, a designated area around the polling place has been set to prevent election campaigning. No party advertisements are allowed in this area, and Republican and Democratic representatives must also speak with voters outside of it.

Sebastian Tynkkynen, Finland's representative in the European Parliament, posted a photo of his meeting with Prince Reza Pahlavi, writing that the prince's struggle for his people truly inspires him and that he wants to end the Islamic Republic's rule once and for all. Tynkkynen said no to the EU's official policy of appeasement with the mullahs and supported recognizing the voice of the Iranian people for regime change.

Anil Menon, a NASA astronaut, voted in the US midterm elections from the International Space Station. He said he filled out his electronic ballot with a computer and sent it to election officials in Harris County, Texas. According to Menon, all three American astronauts present on the station were able to vote.

In the US midterm elections, all 435 seats in the House of Representatives and 35 Senate seats are up for vote. The outcome of this election will determine control of both chambers and the legislative and oversight path over the Trump administration in the remaining two years of his presidency.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said he considers the likelihood of resuming war between the US and the Islamic Republic higher than reaching an agreement. He added that the outcome of the midterm elections and the future composition of Congress could make Trump's military decisions easier or harder.

Donald Trump told Financial Times that the United States has no immediate plans to attack Iran and considers the current situation with Tehran satisfactory. He added that the US is ready but there may be no reason for an attack and emphasized that indirect talks about Iran's enriched uranium reserves continue. Trump also said more oil is passing through the Strait of Hormuz and the blockade of Iranian ports is weakening Tehran's economy.
Voting ended in Ohio; a close race between two parties for the former JD Vance Senate seat was reported. This report was provided by Maryam Rahmati from Iran International.

The Wall Street Journal reported that the Islamic Republic uses asymmetric warfare tactics, including underwater drones carrying explosives, sticky mines, and small boats, to disrupt ship traffic and oil transport from the Persian Gulf. The newspaper cited regional officials and military experts saying Tehran seeks to regain control of the Strait of Hormuz and increase pressure on the Donald Trump administration through these methods. In recent weeks, Islamic Republic forces have fired rocket grenades and attached explosives to commercial ships in addition to using underwater drones.

Michigan, an industrial state in the US and a key state in the 2016 and 2024 presidential elections, is tonight the scene of a Senate seat race. Abdul, the Democratic candidate, if victorious, will become the first Muslim senator in US history.

Roy Cooper, the Democratic Party candidate, won the North Carolina Senate seat in the US midterm elections and delivered a victory speech to his supporters at the Marriott Hotel in Raleigh. With Cooper's victory, Democrats won the state's Senate election for the first time since 2008. This victory is important for the Democrats' efforts to gain a majority in the Senate, although the final results of the congressional races in several states are still unknown.

Shahram Khaledi, a researcher of Middle Eastern history and international relations, said that Israel's shift away from past social-democratic tendencies toward the right, alongside the U.S. Democratic Party's shift to the left, has influenced American voters' views of Israel.

Omid Memarian, journalist and political analyst, referring to the Republican defeat in the US midterm elections, said Donald Trump might resort to a severe and striking military action against the Islamic Republic to end the war faster. According to Memarian, Trump might seek to record a military achievement and declare victory before the new Congress begins and Democratic oversight increases.

Donald Trump did not accept responsibility for the performance of Republican candidates as Democrats increased their seats in the midterm elections. He wrote on Truth Social that his name was not on the ballot, and if it had been, they would have won by a large margin. Associated Press reported that Trump, who followed the results with political advisors and cabinet members at the White House, had campaigned for many Republican candidates before the elections and asked voters to imagine his name was on the ballot.

Josh Shulman, a Democratic member of the Virginia Beach City Council, emphasized in an interview with Kambiz Tavana that dissatisfaction with the president's performance, even among some Republicans, has increased people's motivation to participate widely in the elections.

CNN and CBS networks announced that based on their assessment, the Democrats have gained the majority of seats in the US House of Representatives. NBC network also predicted that this party will control the House with 241 seats against 191 seats for the Republicans.
James Talarico, the Democratic candidate, ended Republican dominance in Texas by winning the Senate election. This is the first victory for a Democrat in a statewide Texas election since 1994.

Donald Trump acknowledged that the war with Iran played a role in the Republicans' defeat in the Tuesday midterm elections. He told Fox News that Democrats will send "crazy" bills to the White House for signature and he will veto them. Trump also said people probably could not accept the short-term gasoline price consequences after the Iran war and announced he does not intend to change his cabinet composition.

With the continued counting of votes in the US midterm elections, Democrats succeeded in gaining the Senate majority and reclaiming control of this chamber from Republicans after two years. Preliminary results also indicate Democrats leading in the House of Representatives; estimates show the party is on the verge of controlling both chambers of Congress.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Speaker of the Islamic Consultative Assembly, described the Democrats' success in the US midterm elections as the American people's "no" to war. Ghalibaf said Americans said no to war either because of conscience or living costs, and we support this message. He warned that if the US government betrays its people's will, Iran's "no" will bring a nightmare.

Alireza Salimi, a member of the Parliament's presidium, said on Wednesday, 13 Aban, that the Islamic Republic today has more power and can strike all US interests in any geographical area it chooses. He added that from the Islamic Republic's perspective, there is no difference between the two US political parties in terms of bullying. Salimi also said that the US election results showed how influential the Islamic Republic is in global equations and even in the internal developments of the US.

Amir Hamidi, a national security expert, said the results of the US midterm elections indicate dissatisfaction among part of the American society with the economic situation and the performance of the Trump administration. He emphasized that the Republican electoral defeat does not mean the end of Trump's power or a strategic weakening of the US. He also warned that a miscalculation by the Islamic Republic in assessing Washington's power could have a heavy cost for Tehran.

Reza Arab, a political analyst, said that the meetings of Prince Reza Pahlavi with members of the European Parliament show that the voice of the Iranian people has been heard in European political circles. He emphasized the need to end Europe's appeasement policy towards the Islamic Republic and said that the plan to overthrow the Islamic Republic, manage the transition period, establish secular democracy, and preserve Iran's territorial integrity were the main focuses of these meetings.

According to American media, Gina Hinojosa, a Democratic member of the Texas State House of Representatives, defeated Greg Abbott, the Republican governor of the state, in the gubernatorial election, ending three decades of Republican control over the position. Hinojosa will be the first Latinx governor of Texas. Democrats are on track to gain control of the House and Senate in this election and have also won in conservative states like South Carolina and Kansas.

The US midterm elections have raised concerns about the future of Washington's relations with Asia-Pacific countries. The war with the Islamic Republic, the energy crisis, and Trump's administration's trade tariffs are main factors behind these concerns. This report is by Alireza Mohibi from Iran International.
The prosecutor of Astara reported the arrest of a citizen in this county due to sending surveillance camera images of the city to foreign media.
A video released by state media shows a group of regime supporters in Tehran threatening to kill the U.S. president with slogans "Khamenei is the leader" and "We will kill Trump."

Alireza Zakani, the mayor of Tehran, said that the United States and Israel have been defeated and cooperating with US plans means artificial respiration to a defeated enemy and preparing the ground for the next attack on Iran. He added that Europe and countries that supported the US in the region owe the Iranian nation and should apologize and compensate for the damages to the Iranian people.

The Kerman Revolutionary Court sentenced three Baha'i citizens, Venus Hosseini-Nejad, Shakila Ghasemi, and Adib Shahbazpour, to a total of 24 years in prison. Each of them was sentenced to eight years in prison. This ruling was issued by the Fifth Branch of the Kerman Revolutionary Court.

A citizen reported to Iran International via a video that they bought two packs of treatment capsules for more than 3.5 million tomans and that it was difficult to afford and pay this amount with a retirement pension.

Joachim Wadephul, Germany's Foreign Minister, identified the Islamic Republic as the main cause of current conflicts and said Tehran's actions have paved the way for military responses from other countries. He stated that the Islamic Republic is preparing to acquire nuclear weapons and supports paramilitary groups in neighboring countries. The German Foreign Minister emphasized that the Islamic Republic's behavior is neither harmless nor friendly and may provoke a military reaction.

The prosecutor of Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari province announced the issuance of an indictment against the principal of the private 'Saoud' school in Shahr-e Kord and other individuals related to the case of a dance video published online. The video shows dancing inside the school, which domestic media described as "behavior unbecoming of an educational environment."
30 students in Miandoab were hospitalized due to symptoms of poisoning. The cause of the poisoning has not yet been determined and the matter is under investigation.

Johan Wadephul, Germany's Foreign Minister, said that due to good relations, Germany's voice is heard in Israel and the US. He added that he does not insist on talks with Iran's Foreign Minister and that regime change in Iran is only possible from within the country. Wadephul also recalled Germany's special responsibility towards Israel.

The head of the Iranian Psychiatric Association stated that rising treatment costs and shortages of psychiatric drugs have led some patients to reduce their medication intake and visit doctors less frequently. Seyed Vahid Shariat said that some psychiatric drugs in the country have become scarce. He warned that reducing or stopping medication could lead to disease relapse and increased hospitalization needs in the coming months.

Rouhollah Rahimpour said the results of the US midterm elections could increase Trump's motivation to end the Islamic Republic case. He added Trump might resort to an imposed agreement on Tehran or a widespread war to achieve this goal.

Morteza Kazemian, a member of Iran International's editorial team, called the statements of the Speaker of the Islamic Republic's parliament about the US elections ironic and shameful. He emphasized that the Islamic Republic has not even allowed a referendum on important national issues. Kazemian also considered the government media's enthusiasm over the Republicans' defeat as stemming from the illusion that the Democrats' victory could change US policy towards the Islamic Republic.
A retiree sent a video to Iran International reporting the price of potatoes and comparing inflation in Iran and the US, saying: "Let's judge which economy has collapsed and who has failed."

Shin Bet announced that preliminary information indicates possible foreign funding and extensive interference in Israel's elections involving "thousands and possibly more". The agency said the financial sources for these activities came from foreign countries and actors with "hidden and even hostile interests." Itamar Ben-Gvir called for the arrest of Arab party leaders and the immediate halt of final election result certification.

Ziaeddin Aghajanpour, head of the Ideological-Political Organization of the Ministry of Defense, said at the November 4 ceremony in Karaj that the Ministry of Defense and the armed forces have produced astonishing weapons, and their missiles can target areas beyond the Middle East. He also warned that if the Americans do not stop their mischief, all American interests in the region will be targeted. Aghajanpour referred to the killing of Ali Khamenei at the beginning of the 40-day war and said he was among the special saints of God.

Hamidreza Moghaddamfar, advisor to the commander of the IRGC, said at the November 4 ceremony in Bandar Abbas that if countries like the UAE and Bahrain provide bases for attacks on Iran to the US, the IRGC's attacks will be beyond just targeting bases and will be more instructive. He added that the IRGC's responses will no longer be proportional and will target the assets of their enemies. He also warned that if Iranian commanders and leaders are targeted, the enemies should expect their own commanders and leaders to be killed.

The Democratic Party took back the majority in the Senate and House of Representatives from Republicans in the US midterm elections. Based on announced results, Democrats have so far taken 54 Senate seats, while Republicans have obtained 42 seats.

Roland Lescure, the French Minister of Economy and Finance, said on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, in response to the Republican defeat in the US midterm elections, that President Donald Trump still has the authority to make decisions on foreign policy and his behavior is unpredictable. Lescure told French TV channel BFM that Trump either decides to rise above political conflicts and reduce his intervention in international affairs, or he does not. He added that this is an issue that needs to be closely monitored in the coming days.

According to reports, Abdul El-Sayed, a Democratic candidate, won the Michigan State Senate seat in the US midterm elections, becoming the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. Media outlets predicted that El-Sayed, 42, defeated Mike Rogers, a Republican candidate backed by Donald Trump, and retained the seat of retiring Democratic Senator Gary Peters for his party. El-Sayed had previously called Israel's war in Gaza "genocide" and opposed war against the Islamic Republic.

Some Iran International viewers criticized the Islamic Republic officials' stance on the US midterm election results in response to the Democrats' victory. They pointed out that with two years remaining in Donald Trump's presidency, the change in congressional majority does not necessarily mean a change in US policies towards the Islamic Republic.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh said Trump is under pressure to end the war with the Islamic Republic quickly to avoid repeating the Republican defeat in the next election. He rejected the possibility of a minimal agreement between Tehran and Washington and added that Trump must either achieve regime change in Iran or eliminate the threat capability of the Islamic Republic and the Revolutionary Guards.

Parliament members approved articles in a bill titled "Combating the infiltration of intelligence services and foreign governments or institutions" allowing courts to punish or dissolve a legal entity if a crime is committed using its name or facilities. Also, if a person commits a criminal act due to negligence harming national security or interests, they face a fifth or sixth degree punishment. If two or more conspire to commit crimes under this bill, each person's punishment can increase by one to two degrees.

Hamidreza Hajibabaei, the deputy speaker of the parliament, said at the November 4, 2026 ceremony in Tabriz that if the US takes action again, all energy and non-energy bright spots used by the US will be targeted. He added that anyone who facilitates the US will be within the Islamic Republic's target circle. The deputy speaker emphasized that helping the US means hostility towards the Iranian nation.

A video released on social media shows that the mother of the late Atefeh Abed spoke at her daughter's grave, saying she wore a dress she had worn on 18 and 19 Dey and walked beside her daughter with it. Atefeh Abed, 23, was targeted during the protests on 19 Dey 1404 in Mashhad.

Amirhossein Mousavi, a political prisoner held in Evin Prison, was sentenced by Branch 15 of Tehran Revolutionary Court to five years in prison and death for the charge of "corruption on earth." This sentence was communicated to him on 13 Aban. He was also sentenced to five years in prison for the charge of "insulting the sacred."

Mohammad Manan Raeisi, the representative of Qom in the parliament, wrote in a message addressed to Masoud Pezeshkian and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf that several days have passed since the threat to the life of the community's Imam by the Israeli enemy, and so far there has been no reaction from them. He criticized their silence and called for a decisive response to the threats. Manan Raeisi also suggested that if there is no access to the White House, the palaces of their regional henchmen should be targeted.

Iranian media published a message attributed to Mojtaba Khamenei stating that hoping for a change in US behavior through party shifts or concessions is a "mistake." The message, released on 13 Aban, describes any concessions to the US as encouraging further demands and wars. Masoud Pezeshkian also emphasized that Mojtaba Khamenei has given new powers to the government for negotiations with the US.

The domestic production of super gasoline has started to be offered at gas stations in Iran; the CEO of the National Refining and Distribution Company announced its price as 103,000 tomans per liter and said that more than 70 stations have been equipped to offer it. The commercial manager of the National Distribution Company stated that the final price of super gasoline ranges between 103,000 to 110,000 tomans depending on transportation costs.

Ata Mohamad, an international relations expert, said that the shift of the congressional majority towards the Democrats does not necessarily lead to reduced pressure from Washington on Tehran. He added that Donald Trump might increase pressure on the Islamic Republic both diplomatically and militarily to achieve results.

Morteza Kazemian, a member of Iran International's editorial team, considers Mojtaba Khamenei's message as a collection of delusions, threats, slogans, and ideological positions and evaluates it as irresponsible from the perspective of national interests and the rights of the Iranian people. Kazemian assesses Mojtaba Khamenei's stance on the US elections as meaning an increased likelihood of renewed war and worsening economic crisis in Iran. He says the root of the crisis is the Islamic Republic and the ultimate solution lies with the Iranian people.

Shahram Khaledi said that the maximum pressure of the US against the Islamic Republic will continue for the next two years, and the Trump administration will neither withdraw military presence in the region nor stop economic pressure on Tehran. He added that Tehran's interpretation of the Democrats' victory as a sign of Trump's weakness could lead to intensified confrontations.

On Tuesday, 12 Aban, a group of greenhouse farmers from Golshan County held a protest in front of the Agriculture Jihad Organization building in Sistan and Baluchestan province in Zahedan. These citizens demanded solutions to problems related to fuel supply and allocation of their required quota.

An image sent to Iran International shows the tombstone of Amirhossein Ebrahimi, a protester executed by the Islamic Republic. Mizan News Agency reported the execution of Amirhossein Maleki and Amirhossein Ebrahimi in Isfahan. With these two executions, the number of those executed in connection with the "Alikhani Square" case reached 9.

Saeed Bashirtash, head of the Central Council of the Seven Aban Front, said the presence of Reza Pahlavi as a guest of the largest faction in the European Parliament was very important. He added that the main message of the speech was to convey the voice of the Iranian people and emphasize that the Islamic Republic is a serious threat not only to Iran but also to European countries and the international community. Bashirtash said European officials should end the policy of appeasement with the Islamic Republic and support the Iranian people.

Reports about reactions to the US election results on Wednesday 13 Aban have been published. It was said that Qalibaf referred to the American people's 'no' to war and that the Iranian people have suffered due to half a century of war-mongering by the Islamic Republic. It was also reported that Netanyahu was on the verge of ending the war with the Islamic Republic but Trump prevented it, and the Iranian people are paying the price for this political game.

Jean-Noël Barrot, France's foreign minister, said the Republican Party's defeat in the US midterm elections showed that democracy in the country is still alive. He added that this result should not divert Europe's attention from protecting its own interests, and if it does, it would be a serious mistake. Barrot emphasized the necessity of ensuring national independence and creating a stronger, more prosperous, and more democratic Europe.

The mother of Erfan Rezaei, a protester killed in the 1401 uprising, said in a video that her son loved life and consciously went to the streets. Azadeh Al-Ayoub had described the protesters as "drunk" individuals who threatened local residents.

Following the Republican defeat in the US midterm congressional elections, many questions have been raised about the possible impact of this defeat on Trump's campaign in Iran. Trump has said that the war with Iran played a role in the Republicans' defeat but he will veto the Democrats' plans. Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, has analyzed this issue in the Payvast program.

Mohammadreza Asprorin, head of the Alborz Province School Builders Charity Assembly, announced that the province still faces a shortage of 4,000 classrooms. Hassan Mehrani, CEO of this assembly, also reported a high density of students and a significant number of double-shift schools in the province. Mohammadreza Alborzi, governor of Chaharbagh County, said the county needs to build 22 new schools to meet the educational needs of students.

Hours after the Republicans' defeat in the US elections, Mojtaba Khamenei opposed any concessions and agreement with the US. At the same time, Trump, defending an attack on Iran, did not rule out the start of a third war with the Islamic Republic and said this decision would be in America's favor.

Real Madrid announced that Rafael Nadal, the Spanish tennis legend, has accepted the offer to join the club's board of directors. The final appointment depends on the approval of the club members' assembly on November 21. Nadal, 40, retired from professional tennis and is a longtime Real Madrid fan.

It was reported that yesterday, Kaveh Osmani, a citizen from Baneh county, was arrested by intelligence officers in this county and transferred to one of the detention centers of this security agency in Sanandaj.

Harana news agency reported the identification of Vahid Khodarikha, 34, one of three arrested protesters in Mashhad who have been sentenced to death on charges of "waging war against God." With his identification, the identities of two of the convicted individuals in this case have been confirmed, but the identity of the third person remains unknown. Vahid Khodarikha, along with Matin Farnian, 23, and another citizen, have been sentenced to death by the Fifth Branch of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court headed by Judge Hossein Yazdankhah in a joint case.

Reports indicate school closures and threats to deduct students' grades and spending resources to bring them to the November 4th ceremony. This occurs amid increased militarization and security atmosphere in schools.
The deputy commander of Fars police reported the arrest of a citizen in Shiraz for reasons including participation in the protests of Dey 1404, connections with opposition groups, and foreign media.

Andy Burnham, the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, said the results of the US midterm elections show that voters want to focus on the issue of living costs. Burnham added that he feels the world now has an opportunity to unite around the issue that affects all our lives, which is the cost of living.
A video received shows that during the compulsory November 4 march in Shahr-e Kord, a group of students responded to the government's slogans by chanting "Long live the Shah."

Following the death of Jesus de Miguel, the 30-year-old forward of Tenerife, major European football clubs paid tribute to him by publishing messages. A minute of silence was also held in stadiums and fans commemorated the player.

Kazem Alinejad, a political prisoner in Evin Prison, started a hunger and medication strike on 13 Aban in protest of being deprived of medical services and proper medical care. Prison officials have promised medical leave but have not fulfilled it. His diabetes has progressed, and doctors continue to prescribe previous medications without specialized examination.

Mohsen Rezaee, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, said the great Iranian nation imposed a major strategic defeat on Trump in the battlefield and the Strait of Hormuz, as well as a heavy political defeat in Washington. He added that American citizens and the government personally bore the heavy costs of Trump's warmongering. Rezaee said anyone who confronts the Islamic Republic of Iran will pay a heavy price from the battlefield to their doorstep.

JD Vance, the US Vice President, identified the war with Iran as a main reason for the Republican defeat in the midterm congressional elections and said many voters who supported Donald Trump and him in 2024 voted for Democratic candidates this time. He stated that ending the war, focusing on living costs and inflation, prioritizing US interests, and changing the country's relationship with Israel were the four main demands of dissatisfied Republican voters. Vance also defended those in the Republican Party who called for a diplomatic resolution to the conflict with Iran and said criticism of support for a diplomatic solution was incorrect.

Mohsen Rezaee, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, reacted to the results of the US midterm elections by writing that the Iranian nation imposed a strategic defeat on Trump in the battlefield and the Strait of Hormuz, and Americans had to pay the cost of his war. He added that anyone who confronts Iran will pay the price. Meanwhile, Iranian media published a message attributed to Mojtaba Khamenei stating that hoping for a change in US behavior through party shifts or concessions is a mistake.

Mohammad Qaedi, an international relations instructor, said the results of the US election go beyond a protest vote against Donald Trump and indicate the formation of a newer and younger identity within the Democratic Party. He stated that Republicans are now facing the challenge of redefining their political position. Qaedi emphasized that Trump must understand the message of the election and avoid repeating George Bush's mistake of ignoring voters' opposition to continuing the Iraq war.

Reports from schools in Hamedan, Tehran, Arak, and Eslamshahr indicate that students and teachers have been pressured to participate in the November 4, 2026, march and threatened with grade reductions or dismissal. Teachers report strict supervision by the education ministry and the influence of regime-affiliated forces in school management. Some students and teachers mention being taught political anthems and required to attend gatherings.

A video received by Iran International shows a group of schoolgirls singing the anthem "Nam-e Javid Vatan" together. In a significant number of schools across the country, singing this anthem has become one of the students' protest actions.

Agence France-Presse reported that the postponement of the 2027 AFC Asian Cup from January to December has made Hajime Moriyasu's future with the Japan national team uncertain. Moriyasu, who was supposed to step down after the tournament, may now hand over his position to Go Oiwa at the end of 2026. He stated that the progress of Japanese football is more important than his personal situation.

Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections and gaining majority in both houses of Congress has created a new challenge for Donald Trump. The Republicans lost even in their traditional strongholds. Iran war, inflation, and rising fuel prices were among the main concerns of voters.

A political earthquake occurred in the United States and the Democrats won the midterm elections with unprecedented results. Thus, the new US Congress with a Democratic majority can obstruct Trump's decisions, including the war with the Islamic Republic.
A video shows a group of students in Isfahan on Wednesday, 13 Aban, chanting "Long live the Shah" in the streets, coinciding with official ceremonies on that day.

At dawn on Wednesday, 13 Aban, the death sentences of four prisoners, including an Afghan national previously convicted of murder, were carried out. The executions of three of these prisoners were reported at Qezel Hesar prison in Karaj.

At least two protest gatherings were held in Tehran and Zahedan. On Wednesday, 13 Aban, literacy movement educators from various provinces gathered in front of the Ministry of Education in Tehran to protest job uncertainty. Yesterday, some greenhouse owners from Golshan county gathered in front of the Agriculture Jihad Organization of Sistan and Baluchestan in Zahedan to protest the non-allocation of greenhouse fuel quotas.

Some contract workers of Zahedan Municipality complain about two to three months of unpaid wages and demand payment of their wage claims. Also, some social security retirees in Alborz province criticized the lower amount of arrears paid in Ordibehesht compared to Farvardin.

A video received by Iran International shows that the fourth anniversary of the killing of the martyr Erfan Zamani was commemorated at his grave. He was killed on the evening of 12 Aban 1401 during the revolutionary uprising "Woman, Life, Freedom" in the city of Lahijan.

Prince Reza Pahlavi said in an exclusive interview with Iran International that the Islamic Republic's support for Russia in the Ukraine war and the expansion of Tehran's security threats to European soil have encouraged European countries more than before to change their policies towards the Islamic Republic. He emphasized that Europe's practical support should focus on maintaining Iranians' access to free internet, increasing economic pressures, and monitoring the assets of Islamic Republic officials. Prince Reza Pahlavi also said that for regime change, coordination of internal forces and the joining of military and law enforcement forces to the people are fundamentally important.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, said on Wednesday, 13 Aban, at the White House that he knew from the beginning that the war with the Islamic Republic would affect the midterm election results but it was worth it, and if he could go back, he would not change his decision. He emphasized that the military power of the Islamic Republic has been completely broken and the goal of the military operation was to prevent them from obtaining nuclear weapons. Trump also said the Strait of Hormuz is open.

Two prisoners convicted of drug-related crimes were executed in Khorramabad prison. Also, two death row prisoners in Torbat Jam and Khuzestan were released after the victims' families pardoned them. A judicial official reported that 86 people have been spared from execution in East Azerbaijan since 1402.

Yesterday, the interrogation session of Azar Mansouri, a political activist, was held at Branch Two of Tehran's Security Prosecutor's Office. The case concerns the publication of a statement related to the December protests.

Dmitry Peskov, Kremlin spokesman, said that President Trump is still in power and expressed sincere hope that he continues his peace efforts. He added that the ground has been prepared for continuing negotiations and a new round of trilateral talks will be held soon.

The Iranian Short Film Association protested the issuance of a prison sentence and other punishments against Jafar Panahi. The association criticized judicial and security measures aimed at pressuring the artistic community and called for a legal review of the issued sentences. Jafar Panahi's lawyer announced last week the issuance of a five-year and one-month prison sentence and other penalties.

Chuck Schumer, a senior Democratic Senate official in the US, said on Wednesday, 13 Aban, that the war in Iran "must end" and noted that his party's future majority in Congress could use its control over the government budget to advance this goal. Schumer accused Donald Trump of unstable decision-making and said the American people do not know what they are fighting for in Iran.

Mohammad Hossein Sepehri, a political prisoner, was released today, Wednesday, 13 Aban 1405, after more than three years of imprisonment from Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad. According to the case documents, his release date was set for 18 Mehr 1405, but due to a case filed after he and Javad Lal Mohammadi were beaten inside the prison, his release was delayed by 25 days.

It was reported that the Republicans lost the US elections because Trump accepted mediation from countries like Qatar and Pakistan several times and stopped the war. Trump, by appeasing the Islamic Republic, gave it the opportunity to buy time and prevent Israeli attacks. Trump also thought he could reach an agreement by removing several layers of the Islamic Republic's leaders, but this structure is plagued by apocalyptic thinking from top to bottom.
A video sent to Iran International shows protesters in Tehran posting a notice on a bridge column that reads: "The regime's warmongering = destruction of the nation."

Benjamin Netanyahu, the Prime Minister of Israel, said in a video published on Wednesday, 13 Aban, that radical Islam threatens Israel from outside through the Islamic Republic and its proxy forces, and from inside through Islamist parties supporting "terrorism." He added that this movement is dismantling European countries and a similar threat exists against Israel. Netanyahu said Islamist parties cannot confront this threat.

Gol Gohar women's team scored their second goal against Persepolis yesterday with an exceptional team effort involving only 5 passes from their own goal area. The goal started with a pass from Fatemeh Adeli, followed by skillful passes from Shabnam Behesht and Zahra Alizadeh, who dribbled past the goalkeeper and assisted Afsaneh Chatrnor for the winning goal. This tactical move led to Sirjan's victory and Persepolis's first defeat, 2-1 in favor of Gol Gohar.
A video sent to Iran International shows that on Wednesday, 13 Aban, a sniper was stationed on top of a building for a government rally in Karaj.

Miad Maleki, former head of the US Treasury Department's sanctions targeting office, said that the sanction on the Turkish airport services company may disrupt Iranian flights to this country. According to him, the continuation of this company's services to Iranian planes depends on banking restrictions and the Turkish government's decision. Maleki also said about the sanction on the tanker flag forgery network that this network helped the shadow fleet bypass sanctions using forged documents, and the new sanctions could affect the Islamic Republic's oil exports for years and strengthen Washington's leverage in negotiations.

Alireza Nourizadeh said the Islamic Republic shows no sign of willingness to compromise despite the Republicans' defeat in the US Congress elections. He added that plans for attacks on sensitive targets in the Gulf countries and Israel have been proposed. Nourizadeh warned that targeting Arab leaders could lead to a widespread war in the region.

Abdul El-Sayed, after winning the Michigan Senate race, faces the challenge of fulfilling his promise to improve health insurance. He criticized Donald Trump and JD Vance in his victory speech. Advancing his promises may require cooperation with the federal government.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, said that the missile threats of the Islamic Republic against European countries have increased Western governments' understanding of Tehran's dangers and have caused the positions of Prince Reza Pahlavi in Europe to receive more attention.
